lines: With you in a moment.
Right. Food, rope, salve, boots. If it isn't on the shelf I haven't got it, and if I haven't got it I can't get it.
That's the whole of my patter. Ask me anything else and you'll get an honest answer, which is worse.
Everyone knows who you are. You were on the gallows a fortnight back and then you weren't.
It doesn't change the price of bread.
What were you expecting - a speech?
You'll get charged what everyone gets charged. That's not me being kind. It's me not being bothered.

choices.text: It reads as kind from where I'm standing.

lines: Then this town has set the bar somewhere I'd rather not think about.
Anyway. Shelf's there, and it's thinner than it was.
At the hanging? No. I was here, minding the shop.
Before you make that into something - I'd likely have gone if I hadn't been. Everyone else did.
So I don't get to be the one who refused. I get to be the one who was busy.

choices.text: You didn't have to tell me that.

lines: No. But you'd have found out, and then you'd have wondered what else I was leaving out.
I'd rather be dull and trusted. It's better for trade.
The carters stopped coming up from the valley in the spring. Nobody decided it. They just stopped.
Half of what I sell came up that road. The other half I can only make if somebody brings me the makings.
You've been down there. You're going again. So: bring me timber and stone and I'll pay over the odds for it.
Because I've nobody else to buy from, and a shop with empty shelves isn't a shop.
It's not generosity. It's the only price that gets the job done.
Eight timber and four stone, to start. That's a cart's worth, near enough.
One thing, and I'd rather say it than have you hear it from him. The carpenter wants that same timber for the rebuilding.
So I'm asking for what's left after him, not instead of him. I'd not want it the other way and I'd not get it the other way.

choices.text: Then I'll bring you what's spare.
He might need all of it.

lines: He might, some weeks. Then I go without and the shelf stays thin, and that's the shape of it.
The offer doesn't expire. Come back when the valley's been generous.

choices.text: All right. What's spare is yours.

lines: Then that's an arrangement, not a favour. I'll want it saying that way round.
Bring the whole eight and four together, mind. I've no use for two timber and a promise.

choices.text: Tallow. That's the name over the door.

lines: TALLOW AND SON. My father painted that before he had any children - that's the sort of man he was, certain in advance.
He got me first. Then he got a son, and then the valley got the son, and I got the shop.
I've not repainted it. Everybody knows where the shop is.

choices.text: You could paint over the last two words.

lines: You didn't do it. Don't stand in my shop apologising for the weather.
But - noted. Thank you.
I could. Paint's four coppers and I've a steady hand.
...I know.
Back. Still standing, still solvent.
Shelf's where it was.

choices.text: You said you couldn't get stock.
Tallow. That's the name over the door.

lines: Eight timber and four stone, and I'll take it in one go or not at all.
Sell me the rest of what you're carrying by all means. Just don't sell me the load - I'd have bought my own cart off you and then paid you again for fetching it.
Good. Come back heavy.
Mind the crate on your way out - it's been there four months and it'll be there four more.
That's the lot, and none of it damp. You'd be surprised.
Sixty, and take the salve with you. You've the look of somebody going straight back out.
Same again whenever you've got it. The road's not going to start running on its own.
